title: Communicating Through Barriers: Aphasia and Anxiety
learning_goal: Apply therapeutic communication techniques and appropriate communication models while avoiding nontherapeutic barriers when interacting with a patient who has expressive aphasia.
visual_style: 2D semi-flat limited-animation style with dynamic but constrained movement. Characters express emotion through head turns, nods, subtle posture shifts, and facial expressions. Non-photorealistic rendering, suggestive lip-sync.

appearance.hair: Dark brown hair pulled back into a neat bun
appearance.uniform: Light blue medical scrubs with a stethoscope around her neck
appearance.distinguishing_features: Warm, professional facial expressions with attentive posture

characters.name: Arthur Pendelton

appearance.distinguishing_features: Slight facial droop on the right side, uses left hand predominantly

characters.emotional_baseline: Easily frustrated due to communication barriers, anxious but willing to cooperate if understood

setting.scene_description: A clean, standard hospital room. The patient is sitting up in the hospital bed with the rails raised. A bedside table sits to the right, and a window shows daylight outside.

lighting.source: Natural light from the window mixed with soft overhead fluorescent lighting

background_furniture.name: Hospital bed
background_furniture.description: Standard adjustable hospital bed with white sheets and a light blanket

background_furniture.name: Bedside table
background_furniture.description: Small table with a lamp and a few personal items

background_equipment.name: IV pole
background_equipment.description: Standard IV pole with a saline bag attached

background_equipment.name: Mounted television
background_equipment.description: Large-screen television mounted on the wall

camera.perspective: Slightly off-center, capturing both the nurse standing beside the bed and the patient in the bed

scenes.scene_summary: Nurse Sarah enters the room to assess Arthur, who is agitated and struggling to speak due to aphasia.
scenes.character_actions: Sarah walks up to the bed, offering a warm smile. Arthur is grimacing, gripping his right shoulder with his left hand. He opens his mouth to speak but only produces a frustrated grunt, shaking his head.

dialogue.line: Good morning, Arthur. I'm your nurse, Sarah. I can see you're uncomfortable today.
(Grunts in frustration, points repeatedly to his shoulder and grimaces)
It looks like you're in pain, but I know it's hard to find the words right now. Let's figure this out.

audio.sound_effects: Footsteps approaching, rustling of hospital gown.
audio.ambience: Low hum of hospital ventilation, distant faint beeping.

scenes.scene_summary: Sarah uses interrogating questions and medical jargon, causing Arthur to shut down.
scenes.character_actions: Sarah tilts her head and points to his shoulder. Arthur throws his left hand up in the air in defeat, turns his head away toward the window, and closes his eyes, refusing to look back.

dialogue.line: Why are you getting so frustrated, Arthur? Is the pain radiating toward your distal clavicle?

audio.sound_effects: Hand slapping lightly against the bed mattress.

scenes.scene_summary: Sarah successfully uses visual/referent communication to assess Arthur's pain.
scenes.character_actions: Sarah holds up a clipboard with a FACES pain scale. Arthur looks at it, visibly relaxing. He points with his left index finger to the severe pain face, then taps his right shoulder.

dialogue.line: Let's use this picture board. Can you point to the face that shows how bad it hurts?
(Points to the chart, then to his shoulder)
Thank you, Arthur. An eight out of ten in your shoulder. I will get your pain medication right away.

audio.sound_effects: Paper rustling as the clipboard is presented.

scenes.scene_summary: Sarah gives false reassurance, causing Arthur to become more distressed.
scenes.character_actions: Sarah smiles broadly and pats his arm casually. Arthur aggressively shakes his head 'no', pointing frantically to his shoulder, his eyes wide with anxiety.

dialogue.line: Everything will be fine, Arthur. I'm sure it's just normal soreness. I'll get your scheduled Tylenol.

audio.sound_effects: Rustling of bedsheets as the patient moves frantically.

scenes.scene_summary: After Arthur's pain is managed, Sarah introduces physical therapy, which triggers an emotional barrier.
scenes.character_actions: Sarah stands beside the bed holding a gait belt. Arthur looks at the belt, his eyes widen, and he immediately shakes his head 'no'. He tightly grips the bedrail with his left hand and looks down.

dialogue.line: Arthur, your pain medication should be working now. The physical therapist wants us to try getting out of bed to walk a few steps.
(Shakes head rapidly, refusing to make eye contact)
You don't want to get up right now?

audio.sound_effects: Clinking of the metal buckle on the gait belt.

scenes.scene_summary: Sarah gives unsolicited advice, causing Arthur to become defensive and angry.
scenes.character_actions: Sarah puts her hands on her hips. Arthur glares at her, crosses his working arm over his chest, and leans back stiffly into the pillows.

dialogue.line: If it were me, I'd just do the therapy. You have to try, Arthur, or you're never going to get your strength back.

audio.sound_effects: Fabric shifting as Arthur crosses his arms.

scenes.scene_summary: Sarah changes the subject, leaving Arthur feeling ignored and anxious.
scenes.character_actions: Sarah waves her hand dismissively and points to the television. Arthur drops his hand from the bedrail, looking confused and defeated, his anxiety visibly unresolved.

dialogue.line: Well, let's not worry about therapy right now. What would you like to watch on TV this afternoon?

scenes.scene_summary: Sarah shares observations to address Arthur's fear, establishing a therapeutic connection.
scenes.character_actions: Sarah leans in slightly, speaking softly. Arthur looks up, nods slowly, and mimics a falling motion with his hand. Sarah nods back reassuringly. Arthur gives a small smile and a thumbs up.

dialogue.line: I notice you look very worried when I mention walking. Are you afraid of falling?
I understand. I will be right beside you holding this belt the entire time. We will only go at your pace.

audio.sound_effects: Soft rustling as Sarah steps closer to the bed.

decision_points.question_text: Arthur is experiencing a physical barrier to communication due to expressive aphasia. How should Sarah assess his pain?

choices.text: Use visual/referent communication, like a FACES pain scale, allowing Arthur to point to convey his message.
Ask "why" he is frustrated and use detailed medical terminology to see if he understands where the pain is.
choices.misconception: Interrogating a patient with 'why' questions and using semantic noise (medical jargon) are nontherapeutic communication techniques that cause defensiveness and misunderstandings.

choices.text: Offer reassurance that the pain is normal and rely on providing his scheduled medications.
choices.misconception: Giving false reassurance and automatic responses minimizes the patient's valid concerns and acts as a barrier to accurate clinical assessment.

decision_points.question_text: Arthur is displaying an emotional barrier (fear/anxiety) toward physical therapy. How should Sarah therapeutically respond to his reluctance?

choices.text: Share observations about his worried demeanor and clarify his specific fears about getting out of bed.
Provide advice on what she would do in his situation, emphasizing the negative consequences of skipping therapy.
choices.misconception: Giving personal advice and making judgmental or threatening statements damages the nurse-patient relationship and prevents the patient from setting their own goals.

choices.text: Change the subject to a more pleasant topic, like television, to avoid escalating his anxiety.
choices.misconception: Changing the subject is a nontherapeutic technique that makes the patient feel their concerns are unimportant, leaving the underlying emotional barrier unresolved.
